Clicking the downvoat button should bring up a menu for choosing a reason for downvoating which must be given in order to downvoat.

Explanation and elaboration below:

The problem with downvoats is that they are used on comments and posts that people disagree with, rather than on actually bad content. One of the main reasons that this happens is because downvoating is so easy to do without thought. Just a single rageclick. Requiring users to pick something from a drop down menu, or more generally adding an additional trivial inconvenience to downvoating will make the cognitive cost of downvoating just a little bit greater, and force users to spend a little bit more time considering why they are downvoating. The reasons are stored internally or displayed anonymously. Instead of (+a | -b), it could be something like (+a | -b -c -d).

This suggestion is not intended to entirely get rid of the problem, but mitigate it. It reduces bad downvoat volume by doing three things:

  1. adding a trivial inconvenience to downvoating. That tiny bit of effort to choose something from a dropdown menu may seem small, but it is many times the effort of simply clicking a button. The motivation to downvoat has to be correspondingly higher in order to downvoat. It's operant conditioning.

  2. Gives people slightly more time to think about what they are downvoating for. Some people agree that downvoats should not be used to disagree, but forget in the heat of the moment. They go to downvoat to disagree, and then they remember that they shouldn't be doing that and stop.

  3. It educates new users who don't know that downvoating is not for just disagreeing. This is one big problem with reddit. There is nothing that new users must go through that teaches them this.

Moderators (or "voatherders") should be able to change that dropdown menu or remove it entirely, because some subverses might want to have fast and loose meme-y bullshit, or might want to allow downvoats for subverse specific reasons (for example, on the r/Scholar subreddit, where you ask for journal articles, and people with access post them for you, you downvote your own post when someone gets the article for you in order to clear the front page of satisfied queries). This downvoating with reasons should be the default though.

(you could also do something silly like giving an option "because I disagree," and when you click it, it gives you a message explaining why you shouldn't do that, and locks the downvoat button for that comment/post) (this is a bad idea)

(you can do fancy things like taking those reasons for downvoating, and comparing them across users downvoating the same post. If one user's downvoats disagree with other downvoats frequently, then their downvoats could get devalued (and of course they get a message that this is happening). There are probably other ideas in this area for finding bad downvoats.)
Downvoats should require a reason for downvoating
You should also add a trivial inconvenience to upvoating so we know the reason behind the upvoat rather than it becoming simply an "I agree" button.

I agree with your intention of giving a 'cost' to downvoates, but I think you suggestion is inapplicable. Instead, I've seen several users suggest that downvoats should decrease the user's ccp or scp (eg1, eg2, eg3).
